Established in 1968,{{cite web |title=Basketball: «Dynamo est une équipe expérimentée» |url=http://akeza.net/basketball-dynamo-est-une-equipe-experimentee/ |website=AKEZA Burundi |accessdate=31 October 2019 |language=French |date=25 October 2017}} the team competes in both the [[Burundian Basketball Championship|Viva Basketball League]] and the Bujumbura Amateurs Basketball Club Association (ACBAB). Dynamo has won the Burundian championship four times, the last time being in 2025. In the [[2024 BAL season|2024 season]], Dynamo played in the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL) as the first team from Burundi to play in the league. After winning their opening game, the team was forced to withdraw after it refused to wear a logo advertising Rwanda, over political reasons. == History == Dynamo Basketball Club was established and founded in 1968. On 25 September 2016, Dynamo won its first-ever [[Burundian Basketball Championship|Burundian National Championship]].{{Cite web |title=Basketball : Dynamo sacré champion national – IWACU |url=https://www.iwacu-burundi.org/basketball-dynamo-sacre-champion-national/ |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=www.iwacu-burundi.org}} In the 2017–18 season, Dynamo had a historically successful season, winning the ACBAB title, [[Heroes' Cup (Burundi)|Heroes' Cup]], and [[President's Cup (Burundi)|President's Cup]].{{cite web |last1=Mugisha |first1=Hervé |title=Dynamo, l'aboutissement… |url=https://www.iwacu-burundi.org/basketball-dynamo-laboutissement/ |website=IWACU Burundi |accessdate=31 October 2019 |language=French |date=31 December 2018}} Their Bujumbura title was their first since 20 years earlier, in 1998.{{Cite web |last=Bukuru |first=Pacifique |date=2018-07-30 |title=Basketball: Dynamo, sacré champion de Bujumbura après 20 ans dans l'ombre |url=https://jimbere.org/basketball-dynamo-sacre-champion-de-bujumbura-apres-20-ans-dans-lombre/ |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=Jimbere |language=fr-FR}} The team captured another ACBAB championship in 2019. Dynamo also qualified for the [[2020 BAL Qualifying Tournaments]].{{cite web |last1=Mugisha |first1=Hervé |title=Dynamo et Les Gazelles sur le toit du basketball national |url=https://www.iwacu-burundi.org/dynamo-et-les-gazelles-sur-le-toit-du-basketball-national/ |website=IWACU Burundi |accessdate=31 October 2019 |language=French |date=26 August 2019}} === Recent years === {{See also|2023–24 Dynamo BBC season}} Dynamo won their fourth national championship in 2023.{{Cite news |date=2023-08-17 |title=Kenya Moran's Ariel Okal celebrate sixth league title as Dynamo edge out holders Urunani in Burundi |url=https://www.afrobasket.com/Kenya/news/824764/Kenya-Morans'-Ariel-Okal-celebrates-sixth-league-title-as-Dynamo-edge-out-holders-Urunani-in-Burundi |archive-date= |access-date=2023-08-17 |work=Afrobasket}} They then played in the [[2024 BAL qualification|2024 BAL qualification tournament]], and on 26 November 2023 they clinched their participation in the [[2024 BAL season|2024 season]] of the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL).{{Cite web |date=2023-11-26 |title=Dynamo outlast COSPN, secure last BAL ticket |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/africaleague/2024/qualifiers/news/dynamo-outlast-cospn-secure-last-bal-ticket |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} Dynamo defeated the Malagasy team [[COSPN]] 79–78 in the third place game, became the first team from Burundi to play in the league, and the first Elite 16 wild card to advance to the main tournament. In the opening day game between Dynamo and South Africa's [[Cape Town Tigers]], the Burundian side taped off the logo of league sponsor Visit Rwanda. [[Burundi–Rwanda relations|Political tensions between the two border nations Burundi and Rwanda]] had been rising, as Burundi has accused Rwanda of supporting the [[RED-Tabara]] rebel militia in the country.{{Cite news |date=2024-03-12 |title=Burundi's Dynamo exit Basketball Africa League over jersey row |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/burundis-dynamo-withdrawn-basketball-africa-league-over-jersey-row-2024-03-12/ |access-date=2024-03-14 |work=[[Reuters]]}}{{Cite web |date=2024-03-12 |title=Burundi's Dynamo BC out of BAL over Visit Rwanda protest |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/39713730/burundi-dynamo-bc-bal-visit-rwanda-protest |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} Dynamo forfeited their second game against FUS Rabat on 10 March, with the BAL citing "refusing to comply with the league’s rules governing jersey and uniform requirements" as the reason why.{{Cite web |title=Dynamo Basketball Club forfeits game against FUS Rabat Basketball |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/dynamo-basketball-club-forfeits-game-against-fus-rabat-basketball |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=The BAL |language=en}} Following Dynamo's second forfeit on 12 March, the team was automatically withdrawn from the group as per FIBA rules.{{Cite web |date=2024-03-12 |title=Basketball Africa League President Amadou Gallo Fall Statement regarding Dynamo Basketball Club |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/basketball-africa-league-president-amadou-gallo-fall-statement-regarding-dynamo-basketball-club |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=The BAL |language=en}} Dynamo players Bryton Hobbs and [[Makhtar Gueye (basketball)|Makhtar Gueye]] stated that the Burundian government had prohibited the team to wear the logo and ordered the club to forfeit its games if necessary.{{Cite web |last=Reporter |first=Times |date=2024-03-11 |title=BAL 2024: Gueye slams Burundi's interference amid Dynamo forfeit |url=https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/15163/sports/football/bal-2024-gueye-slams-burundis-interference-amid-dynamo-forfeit |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=The New Times |language=en}} The following year, ''Les Verts'' were unable to play in the BAL qualifiers, as they lost to Urunani in the finals. In the 2025 season, Dynamo defeated Urunani in seven games in the finals to win the national championship for a fourth time.{{Cite web |title=Febabu/Clôture des Play-offs 2025: Dynamo sacré champion 2025 après avoir éliminé Urunani – Actualités sur le Burundi |url=https://lerenouveau.bi/febabu-cloture-des-play-offs-2025-dynamo-sacre-champion-2025-apres-avoir-elimine-urunani/
